svg.title: HOW MUCH DOES THE CLOCK MATTER?
svg.desc: Five deterministic release times spanning ten days around each of forty central Drake surface releases. Central tracks are thin lines; completed shifted endpoints are dots and terminated trials are crosses. Deterministic release-time shifts test pathway phase sensitivity only. Equal trial counts are not probability, frequency, water-mass volume, residence, or heat transport.
svg.metadata: Native OSCAR field SHA-256 4e8097deef965b3156617be10cc7b40252bfbfdfc6fda7e1f23a7c9f6faff42d; Natural Earth commit ca96624a56bd078437bca8184e78163e5039ad19, SHA-256 9e0729ee253ca7d7a5c4ae9395fb1902264c5377c52e224d13dd85010e2835d9. No diffusion or random sampling.
svg.text: OSW / MOTION STUDY · M2 RELEASE-TIME SENSITIVITY
HOW MUCH DOES THE CLOCK MATTER?
40 central releases · five deterministic starts from −5 to +5 days · 200 native-grid tracks · no diffusion
DOT = COMPLETED SHIFTED-TIME ENDPOINT · × = TERMINATED TRIAL END · OPEN CIRCLE + THIN LINE = CENTRAL RELEASE · COLOR = RELEASE POSITION NORTH → SOUTH
